name: LinkSwift
tagline: A browser script that finds the real download link on Chinese cloud-storage pages so you can use your own download tool.
sentence: Install one script in your browser, open a Baidu or Aliyun cloud-storage shared link, and it shows the direct download address - so you can grab the file with any download manager instead of the provider's app.

board.say: Someone sends you a file on Baidu, Aliyun, or another Chinese cloud drive, and you have to install their app to download it at a reasonable speed.
You open the shared link in your browser, where the LinkSwift script is already installed.
The cloud-storage shared link someone gave you.
The script reads the page and finds the file's real download address.
steps: Detects which cloud provider the page belongs to (Baidu, Aliyun, Quark, Xunlei, UC, 123 Cloud, China Mobile Cloud, or Tianyi Cloud)
Calls the provider's own public download interface to get the direct file link
Shows a download button with the direct link on the page

board.say: A direct download link you can use with any download manager.

outputs.eg: A full URL you can paste into your browser's download bar, IDM, or any download manager
Download the file directly instead of installing the Baidu Netdisk desktop app

before: You have to install the cloud provider's desktop app just to download a file someone shared
Downloads through the web interface are throttled to slow speeds without a paid plan
Each provider has its own app, so you end up with 3-4 apps for occasional file downloads
after: One browser script covers 8 cloud providers - no apps to install
Direct download links work in any download manager or browser
No account or login needed for files shared with a public link
uses_note: LinkSwift has 36.5K stars and has been on GitHub since 2022, but no independent English-language use reports were found. The user base is primarily Chinese-speaking.

steps: Install the [Tampermonkey extension](https://www.tampermonkey.net/) in your browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, or Safari)
[Install LinkSwift](https://github.com/hmjz100/LinkSwift) from GitHub by clicking the user.js file and hitting 'Install' in Tampermonkey
Open a shared file link on [Baidu Pan](https://pan.baidu.com/) or any other supported cloud drive - the script adds a download button to the page
try.paste:
/skillspector https://github.com/hmjz100/LinkSwift
Then: Read the README for install instructions and test with a Baidu cloud-storage shared link.

footprint.disk: A single JavaScript file, under 1 MB. Runs inside your browser's Tampermonkey extension.
footprint.memory: Runs inside a browser tab - no separate process.
footprint.runs_on: Any browser that supports Tampermonkey or Violentmonkey: Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari. Works on desktop only.

best_for: Anyone who receives files shared through Chinese cloud-storage services and wants to skip installing the provider's app
People who prefer using their own download manager instead of the provider's client
skip_if: You don't use Chinese cloud-storage services (Baidu, Aliyun, etc.)
You already have the provider's desktop app and are fine with it
You need to upload or sync files, not just download

alternatives.name: Motrix
alternatives.line: A free download manager that can use direct links once you have them

alternatives.name: baiduyun (original)
alternatives.line: The original userscript LinkSwift is based on - Baidu-only, no longer actively maintained

watch: **Based on another developer's work.** LinkSwift is a modified version of the original script by syhyz1990. The README does not clarify whether the original author consented to the fork.
**Chinese-language only.** The entire interface, documentation, and community are in Chinese.
**Cloud providers change their systems.** Direct-link scripts break when a provider updates its download API. The project has been maintained since 2022, but breaks are common.

**Legal gray area.** Extracting direct download links may violate some providers' terms of service. The project states it uses public APIs and does not bypass speed limits, but provider policies vary.
